title: Not noticing titles; first Jelly Roll session

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Just like I say, when I was recording, I never paid too much attention to the titles, because a lot of that stuff I never figured would be history, you know.
Yeah. Well, of course.
Like I forgot a lot of them tunes I made with Jelly, because I was just on a recording date.
Yeah.
Now looking back, 50 years later --
Just another gig, huh?
Yeah.
Well, did you know what to expect when you recorded with Jelly? Had you heard any of his records, or you just --
No, I hadn't heard any of his records. In fact, I didn't know him. Until I got there, went to the session that day.
That was done for Victor, too.
Uh-huh.
It was a different place, though, back then?
That was a different place.
That's the one, I think that was, near the Drake Hotel.
Yeah, just across the street on Michigan Avenue, Michigan and Oak?
Somewhere like that.
Somewhere like that.
But you didn't know what to expect?
NO.
Was it a morning session, or afternoon session, basically?
Afternoon.
Did you know any of the other guys on the date?
Yeah, well, I knew Omer Simeon. And Shirley Clay, trumpet player. And I didn't know Mitchell real well, but, you know, I knew him casually.
George Mitchell?
George Mitchell.
But Johnny and Baby Dodds were on --
They were on some of those sessions, too.
Did you know them before that session?
No, I'd heard them, but I didn't know them. That's the first time working with them.
Well, you say you didn't know Jelly before then. Had you heard anything by him?
No, I hadn't even heard anything by him.
Did you have any contact with him after the sessions?
I don't remember. I don't think so. Because I think he left town after that.
Yeah, I guess he did, a year or so after that, then he went to New York. Do you remember the diamond tooth in his --
Yeah, I remember the diamond tooth.
